claims: Annual leave payouts are taxed as ordinary income at the employee's marginal tax rate. The ATO does not apply any concessional treatment to annual leave payouts. ... the pre-16 August 1978 component is taxed at 5%, and the post-1978 component is taxed at the marginal rate.
whys: ATO rules: unused annual leave accrued before 18 Aug 1993, or paid out in a genuine redundancy, invalidity or approved early retirement, is taxed at a maximum of 30% plus Medicare levy. For long service leave, only 5% of the pre-16 Aug 1978 amount is added to assessable income (it is not taxed at a 5% rate), and the 16 Aug 1978 to 17 Aug 1993 portion is capped at 30% plus Medicare levy. The leave-calculator.tsx tax note also says long service leave 'may qualify for concessional tax treatment', which contradicts this paragraph.
constants: Unused leave payment tax rules (ATO 'Unused leave payments on termination') should sit in a tax constants file, e.g. lib/constants/australian-tax.ts

claims: The table below summarises the 3 leave types with cash value on termination: annual leave, personal/carer's leave, and long service leave.
whys: Personal/carer's leave has no cash value on termination (the table's own row says 'No: no cash value', and line 291 says it has zero cash value). The table also shows 7 rows, not 3.
The SG rate is typed into the prose (also on line 305). It should render from SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate so that it updates when the rate changes.

claims: Australian employees are entitled to 7 distinct types of leave
whys: The 7-row table counts annual leave twice (standard and shift workers) and leaves out NES family and domestic violence leave (10 days paid). The count does not match the NES list.

claims: a part-time employee working 25 hours per week accrues 2.63 weeks of leave per year (25/38 x 4 weeks), not the full 4 weeks
whys: Under the NES a part-time employee accrues 4 weeks of their own ordinary hours (100 hours at 25 h/week). 2.63 is the equivalent in full-time weeks, so saying they do not get 'the full 4 weeks' is misleading. Line 71 ('80 hours (2.1 weeks)' at 20 hours per week) has the same framing.

claims: 2.923 hours of leave per week, or approximately 0.833 days per fortnight
whys: 152 hours / 26 fortnights = 5.85 hours = 0.769 days of 7.6 hours per fortnight, not 0.833. 0.833 days would be about 20 days over 24 periods (half-monthly).
constants: Derive from EMPLOYMENT.annualLeaveWeeks, standardWeeklyHours and weeksPerYear in lib/constants

claims: There is no concessional tax treatment for leave loading, whether it is paid while you take leave or paid out on termination.
whys: Leave loading paid out with unused annual leave in a genuine redundancy, or accrued before 18 Aug 1993, follows the same capped (30% plus Medicare levy) treatment as the leave itself. Same issue on line 292 ('taxed at marginal rates, not at a flat rate').
